[Memory Pressure] Replace MacOS OS pressure signal with ThresholdMemoryPressureEvaluator

Introduce an experimental feature to evaluate macOS system memory
pressure using physical memory byte thresholds via
ThresholdMemoryPressureEvaluator rather than relying on native OS
DISPATCH_SOURCE_TYPE_MEMORYPRESSURE notifications.

This CL adds the kMacAvailableMemoryPressureEvaluator feature with
MacModerateThresholdMB (1200 MiB) and MacCriticalThresholdMB (800 MiB)
as feature parameters, under BUILDFLAG(IS_MAC).

If the feature is enabled, it instantiates
ThresholdMemoryPressureEvaluator as an auxiliary evaluator, and sets
mac::SystemMemoryPressureEvaluator as a shadow evaluator that does not
emit any votes, as it's set with a null voter.

mac::SystemMemoryPressureEvaluator now records the OS signal into a new
Memory.PressureLevel2.OS histogram, on all Apple platforms.

To keep the Disk bucket of Memory.PressureLevel2 accurate when non-OS
voters are active or the OS evaluator runs in shadow mode,
MemoryPressureVoteAggregator now tracks whether critical pressure is
caused solely by the disk voter (via CreateVoter(is_disk_voter)) rather
than relying on the OS and disk evaluators pushing their state to
MultiSourceMemoryPressureMonitor.

[loom] Set dropEffect to none when files can't be added as context

Follow-up to https://crrev.com/c/8615748: while hiding the drag glow
when AI Mode file context cannot be added removes the glow animation,
the OS drag cursor still defaults to the copy (+) cursor.

Wrap the `dragover` listener on `#inputWrapper` so it continues calling
`DragAndDropHandler.handleDragOver` (`preventDefault()` keeps Blink from
navigating the WebContents on drop) and sets
`e.dataTransfer.dropEffect = 'none'` when `!this.canAddFileContext_()`.

[mojo] Measure peak open renderer channels

Measure concurrent Mojo channel usage in Windows renderers to help
assess the capacity required by the proposed event-based I/O pump.

Track channels from successful I/O registration until their pipe handle
closes or is released. Emit each newly reached per-I/O-thread peak
immediately, avoiding reliance on orderly renderer shutdown and
cumulative counts inflated by channel churn.

Restrict collection to renderers through Channel's existing metrics-only
process-type access. This measures open channels, not exact event-watch
occupancy: channels with closed handles and retiring completions are
excluded.

[Clank][ImageWriter] (2c/6) Allow usb-storage detach for internal callers

On Desktop Android (Clank), when an external USB flash drive or SD card
reader is plugged in, the Linux kernel binds the `usb-storage` driver to
its USB Mass Storage Bulk-Only Transport (BOT) interface (Class 0x08,
Subclass 0x06, Protocol 0x50). While `usb-storage` is bound, raw bulk
endpoint transfers via `device.mojom.UsbDevice` fail with `EAGAIN` /
`EBUSY` until the kernel driver is detached via `USBDEVFS_DISCONNECT`.

`UsbDeviceHandleUsbfs::ClaimInterface()` already supports detaching
kernel drivers on Linux/Android via `USBDEVFS_DISCONNECT` (and
automatically reattaching them via `USBDEVFS_CONNECT` on
`ReleaseInterface()`) when `features::kAutomaticUsbDetach` is enabled
and the interface matches `UsbInterfaceDetachAllowlist`.

Add `usb-storage` matching USB Mass Storage SCSI transparent command set
Bulk-Only Transport (`0x08`, `0x06`, `0x50`) to
`UsbInterfaceDetachAllowlist` with `unrestricted_only = true`, and thread
`allow_unrestricted_detach` from `DeviceImpl` (set only when opened via
`UsbDeviceManager::GetUnrestrictedDevice`) through `UsbDeviceHandle` to
`UsbInterfaceDetachAllowlist::CanDetach()`.

Security / WebUSB / IWA impact:
- Untrusted WebUSB origins remain blocked from claiming Mass Storage
  interfaces in `DeviceImpl::ClaimInterface()`.
- Isolated Web Apps with `kUsbUnrestricted` open devices via
  `WebUsbServiceImpl::GetDevice()` -> `UsbDeviceManager::GetDevice()`,
  where `allow_unrestricted_detach` is `false`, so IWAs cannot detach
  `usb-storage`.
- Only internal browser callers using
  `UsbDeviceManager::GetUnrestrictedDevice()` (such as
  `chrome.imageWriterPrivate` for the Chromebook Recovery Utility) have
  `allow_unrestricted_detach = true` and can detach `usb-storage`.

This eliminates the need for `chrome.imageWriterPrivate` on Android to
open a separate `UsbDeviceConnection` via JNI (`crrev.com/c/8612356`) or
perform direct `usbdevfs` `ioctl` transfers (`crrev.com/c/8583374`).

Bug: 538632205
Test: services_unittests --gtest_filter=UsbInterfaceDetachAllowlistTest.*:UsbDeviceHandleUsbfsTest.*:USBDeviceImplTest.*

[ActorSurface] Refactor for ActorSurface in remaining actor tools

A few tools still reached their WebContents through the tab, so they
failed or skipped work on a surface without one (e.g. a headless page).
Use the surface's WebContents instead:

- SiteBasedSearchTool targets an ActorSurfaceHandle.
- ObservationDelayController::Wait takes a WebContents instead of a
  tab. LoadAndExtractContentTool waits on its own page.
- PerformSearchToolRequest::AssociatedOriginGrant gets the profile from
  the page.
- Remove unused TabHandle aliases and includes.

Revert "[ios] Eliminate EDO polling traffic for EarlGrey UI element waits"

This reverts commit 63ae822d5a9f888882daf6085fb25abfca877093.

Reason for revert: Appears to break several tests on iOS, which fail
in "waitForElementWithMatcher" calls:
AgeMismatchSignoutTestCase/testSwitchToAccountCannotSignInTriggersAgeMismatch
AutofillAIEGTest/testSubmitRedressForm
BookmarksFolderChooserAccountTestCase/testEditFunctionalityOnSingleFolderAccount
DeeplinkSigninTestCase/testCrossDeviceSigninInIncognito
PasswordManagerAccountStorageTestCase/testSavePasswordsInAccountFlowCompletesMovingPasswords
PasswordManagerAccountStorageTestCase/testSavePasswordsInAccountFlowCompletesMovingPasswords

Failure Link: https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/ios-simulator-full-configs/87021/overview

Original change's description:
> [ios] Eliminate EDO polling traffic for EarlGrey UI element waits
>
> ChromeEarlGrey UI element wait helpers previously polled from the test
> runner, triggering cross-process EDO calls, failure screenshots, and UI
> hierarchy dumps on every failed poll tick.
>
> Move these waits into the app process via InAppWaiter to poll matchers
> at 50ms in-process and run the final EarlGrey assertion only once
> satisfied. Also swizzle EarlGreyImpl's root matcher setter so in-app
> queries use the active root window matcher.
>

[Clank][ImageWriter] (2b/6) Add SCSI capacity probing for Android USB

Implements SCSI capacity probing for USB Mass Storage Bulk-Only
Transport (BOT) devices in RemovableStorageProvider on Android:

- Adds MojoUsbCapacityReader to query drive capacity via SCSI
  TEST UNIT READY, REQUEST SENSE (to clear UNIT ATTENTION), and
  READ CAPACITY (10) when sysfs capacity is inaccessible due to
  SELinux restrictions.
- Filters out unready or zero-capacity USB candidates before returning
  the device list.
- Adds FakeBotUsbDevice unit tests in
  removable_storage_provider_android_unittest.cc covering
  UNIT ATTENTION recovery and zero/overflow capacity filtering.

Reland "[Extensions] Implement runtime.getDocumentId() API"

This is a reland of commit 28732282004a00c63d4642d84713c347cba46002

What changed in the reland:
- The pre-existing UAF in NavPrefetchBrowserTest (where
  rfhi.GetDocumentToken() was called after a cross-document navigation
  had already destroyed rfhi when BackForwardCache is disabled) was
  fixed separately in crrev.com/c/8616829.
- Added "nodoc": true to runtime.getDocumentId in runtime.json and moved
  the document_id_ assignment into the ExtensionDocumentUserData
  constructor body after the lifecycle CHECK.

Original change's description:
> [Extensions] Implement runtime.getDocumentId() API
>
> This CL implements the synchronous chrome.runtime.getDocumentId()
> extension API which allows extension contexts and content scripts to
> synchronously retrieve the unique document ID of a given WindowProxy or
> frame owner element (iframe, frame, embed, or object), and throws a
> synchronous error if the target is invalid or detached.
>
> To support synchronous renderer-side execution, this CL:
> - Flag-guards this API logic behind a kApiRuntimeGetDocumentId flag
> - Exposes content::RenderFrameHost::GetDocumentToken() and unifies
> ExtensionApiFrameIdMap. Previously,
> ExtensionApiFrameIdMap::ExtensionDocumentUserData created a separate
> random base::UnguessableToken in the browser process that the renderer
> had no knowledge of. Now, we stop generating a separate document ID in
> the browser process and instead just use the existing document token in
> the renderer which ensures the ID will be returned synchronously.
> - Adds blink::WebFrame::FromWindow(): Blink already resolves DOM frame owner elements to a WebFrame*, but it lacked a helper to resolve a V8 Window / WindowProxy value to its corresponding WebFrame*.
> - Implements runtime.getDocumentId() in RuntimeHooksDelegate: The
> schema definition and feature rules are added and
> RuntimeHooksDelegate::HandleGetDocumentId() is implemented.
>
> Cross-origin same-process frames are supported in this CL, but
> out-of-process frames are not supported yet. This will be done in a
> separate CL.
>

[Clank][ImageWriter] (2a/6) Add Android USB and sysfs enumeration

Implements the first part of RemovableStorageProvider on Android:

- Enumerates removable kernel block devices under /sys/block (filtering
  out non-removable internal storage, read-only devices, and virtual
  block prefixes).
- Enumerates USB Mass Storage Bulk-Only Transport (class 0x08, subclass
  0x06, protocol 0x50) devices via device::mojom::UsbDeviceManager,
  checking Android USB permission via RefreshDeviceInfo().
- Adds unit tests in removable_storage_provider_android_unittest.cc for
  endpoint extraction, sysfs block enumeration, and permitted USB device
  enumeration, and wires the provider and unit tests into
  chrome/browser/extensions/BUILD.gn.

[pgo] Disable Mach-O fixup chains for macOS x64 test binaries

Upstream LLD PR https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/233895 added a
diagnostic when a Mach-O segment with chained fixups exceeds the maximum
encodable size in dyld_chained_starts_in_segment::max_valid_pointer. On
macOS x64 (where page_size = 4 KiB and max_pages = 65,536), chained
fixups cannot span a segment larger than 256 MiB.

In macOS x64 PGO instrumentation builds (chrome_pgo_phase = 1 on
ToTMacPGO), Chromium Framework links cleanly with chained fixups
enabled, but large monolithic test binaries (such as
components_unittests, browser_tests, and unit_tests) have __DATA
segments that exceed 256 MiB once __llvm_prf_cnts and __llvm_prf_data
sections are added.

Pass -Wl,-no_fixup_chains for test binaries when chrome_pgo_phase == 1
on macOS x64 so that non-test binaries (including Chromium Framework)
continue to be instrumented with the same chained fixups configuration
that we ship.

[Read Anything] Fix flaky AudioMenuElement accent menu close test

CrDialogElement.close() calls close() on the underlying native <dialog>
element, which schedules its native 'close' event on the next animation
frame via HTMLDialogElement::ScheduleCloseEvent() rather than in a
microtask or 0ms timer.

On slower or heavily loaded bots (such as win11-arm64-rel-tests),
microtasksFinished() can resolve before the next animation frame fires
the dialog's 'close' event, causing the assertion that <accent-menu> is
removed to fail flakily.

Await eventToPromise('close', accentMenu) before microtasksFinished()
(matching the voice selection dialog test below it) and re-enable both
tests in AudioMenuElement.

[iOS] Fix and re-enable testWithUMACheckedAndSigninSupervised

Re-enable the disabled EarlGrey test
testWithUMACheckedAndSigninSupervised in
FirstRunWithoutSearchEngineChoiceTestCase, disabled in
crrev.com/c/5310064 (crbug.com/40070867).

Root cause and fix:
In -[FirstRunTestCaseBase acceptSyncOrHistory], the test selected
chrome_test_util::ButtonStackPrimaryButton() immediately without
waiting for the History Sync screen to be displayed. When signing in
with a supervised account, capability checks introduce an asynchronous
delay before HistorySyncCoordinator presents
HistorySyncViewController. Tapping the primary button immediately raced
with this transition, either hitting the button on the preceding
welcome screen or failing to find an interactable button while the
history sync screen was still appearing.

Update -[FirstRunTestCaseBase acceptSyncOrHistory] to wait for
kHistorySyncViewAccessibilityIdentifier to become sufficiently visible
with waitForSufficientlyVisibleElementWithMatcher: before tapping the
primary button, and use elementInteractionWithGreyMatcher:
scrollViewIdentifier: with kButtonStackScrollViewAccessibilityIdentifier
to guarantee the button is scrolled into view and interactable across
both phone and tablet form factors.

Verified locally:
- iPhone 16 Pro / iOS 27.0: 3/3 passed
- iPad (A16) / iOS 27.0: 3/3 passed
- iPhone 16 Pro / iOS 26.5: 3/3 passed
- iPad (A16) / iOS 26.5: 3/3 passed
Also verified sibling tests calling acceptSyncOrHistory:
testWithUMACheckedAndSignin, testWithUMAUncheckedAndSignin,
testForceSigninByPolicy, and
FirstRunSearchEngineChoiceTestCase's
testSearchEngineChoiceScreenWithSigninNeedsReauth.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

[editing] Fix `TextOffsetMappingTest.BlockInInlineWithAbsolute`

The test bitrotted because of a missing `EXPECT_THAT(results, ...)`
when originally added in https://crrev.com/c/3747613.

When asserted, the test expected 3 elements instead of the actual 5:
1. <p>ab</p>
2. " " in `#t` (after <p>)
3. <a> (out-of-flow positioned element inside <p>)
4. <p> (block-in-inline)
5. <i> in `#t` (before <p>)

The 5-element result is the correct behavior: skipping the
block-in-inline and out-of-flow element would cause text within them to
be omitted during backward range iteration. Additionally, since
https://crrev.com/c/5842631, out-of-flow and floating elements form
their own text segment boundaries instead of merging into the outer
block container.

[Payments] Reset activationless show on user-initiated reload

Previously, PaymentRequestWebContentsManager::DidStartNavigation()
ignored all browser-initiated reloads when deciding whether to reset
had_activationless_show_. That restriction was added to prevent
error_page::NetErrorAutoReloader from resetting the bit after an
unactivated renderer-initiated navigation fails with a network error,
which would otherwise allow a website to bypass the once-per-navigation
activationless show() limit (crbug.com/40072274). However, it also
prevented user-initiated browser reloads (such as pressing the toolbar
refresh button or reload shortcut) from resetting the bit.

Allow browser-initiated reloads to reset had_activationless_show_ unless
the currently committed primary main frame document is an error document
(RenderFrameHost::IsErrorDocument()). Because error-page auto-reloaders
only reload committed error documents, this blocks the auto-reload
bypass while allowing user-initiated browser reloads on normal pages to
reset the activationless show allowance.

Fixed: 40282980
Test: components_unittests --gtest_filter=PaymentRequestWebContentsManagerTest.*

[Transit] Report Conditions blocked on Suppliers as BLKD, not FAIL

When a Condition declared inputs with dependOnSupplier() and an input
has no value yet, the Condition's own check does not run. If the
Transition timed out, the summary still marked it [FAIL] and counted it
as a failure, so one root cause with two dependents read as three
independent failures.

Now such Conditions get the verdict [BLKD] and are listed in a
"⏳ BLOCKED" block between the failed and OK blocks, without their
history. They are not counted as failures in the main message. Each
blocked Condition references the Condition supplying the missing value
by index when it is part of the Transition ("blocked on [5]"),
otherwise by the input name given to dependOnSupplier().

Example:
  Did not complete ..., failed 1 Condition: [1] producer

  ❌ FAILED ENTER <C2001: destination state>:
      [1] [FAIL] producer {unfulfilled after 100 ms}

  ⏳ BLOCKED ENTER <C2001: destination state>:
      [2] [BLKD] dependent on producer {blocked on [1] for 100 ms}
      [3] [BLKD] dependent on outside {blocked on OutsideInput for 100 ms}

The Shared Tabs close button used the same button configuration as the
Assistant AIM header close button but still looked different:
- It was a custom view of a navigation bar button item. The navigation

Lay the button out over the navigation bar instead of as a bar button
item, with the same 40x40 size, 16pt trailing padding, and shadow as the
Assistant AIM header close button.

[Extensions] Defer synced host permissions for outdated extensions

When Chrome Sync receives data indicating an extension is allowed to run
"Always on all sites" (withhold_permissions = false), applying this
immediately can be dangerous if the local extension is outdated (state
== INSTALLED_OUTDATED). Granting these permissions immediately could
accidentally give the older, local version broader access than intended
while it waits to update to the newer synced version.

This CL defers the permission grant. Instead of applying it immediately,
the incoming withhold_permissions = false value is stored in a
PendingUpdate. It is only actually applied (via OnExtensionInstalled)
once the local extension finishes updating to a version at or newer than
the synced version. (This logic is guarded by the
kExtensionInstallSiteAccessOptions flag and disabled by default
currently).

Edge Cases Handled:
- Immediate Restrictions: Restricting permissions
  (withhold_permissions = true) continues to apply immediately to
  outdated extensions.
- Sync Merges: While an update is pending, CreateSyncData reports the
  deferred permission state so MergeDataAndStartSyncing doesn't
  accidentally overwrite the sync server with the outdated local state.
- Pre-setting Preferences: If an outdated extension doesn't currently
  request host permissions, but the synced version restricts them, we
  pre-set the restriction in ExtensionPrefs. This ensures any newly
  added host permissions are withheld the moment the update installs.
- Local Overrides: If a user manually changes permissions locally before
  the extension is fully loaded in ExtensionRegistry, we mark NeedsSync
  so the local change isn't overwritten by sync.
- Updating Past Synced Version: If a local extension updates directly
  to a version newer than the pending synced version, the deferred
  permission grant is still applied (provided the update is not disabled
  due to a permissions increase).

[Android Test Runner] Tighten bounded-load shard cap to 2%

Lower BOUNDED_LOAD_EPSILON from 0.05 to 0.02, so bounded-load hashing
spills a test group off its hash shard once that shard exceeds the mean
estimated load by 2% rather than 5%.

Replaying LocalDeviceTestRun._ApplyExternalSharding over per-test
durations from android-x64-rel ResultDB results, with each real shard's
bot-speed factor normalized out and then re-added by Monte Carlo to get
an expected slowest shard:

chrome_public_test_apk (four full runs, 56 shards, 6,000-7,000 tests):
* Expected slowest shard 864 s -> 844 s (-20 s) with today's
  instrumentation weights, or 807 s -> 794 s on top of
  crrev.com/c/8640357; shard-load standard deviation 97 s -> 83 s.
* 97% of tests keep their shard when 2% of tests are removed, vs 98%
  at 0.05.
* The cap-overflow fallback never triggers at 0.02. At 0.00 it does
  (large batches no longer fit anywhere and land on an arbitrary shard),
  which made even exact per-test weights worse than at 0.02, so 0.02 is
  the floor for this algorithm.

android_browsertests (six full runs, 25 shards, 2,100-2,340 tests):
* Shard-load standard deviation 42.5 s -> 38.3 s (-10%); expected
  slowest shard 546 s -> 542 s; slowest shard with bot speed removed
  unchanged within noise (481 s vs 483 s). With uniform gtest weights
  there is little information for the cap to act on.
* 98% of groups keep their shard when 2% of tests are removed, vs 99%
  at 0.05.

The same replay shows that weight heuristics keyed on gtest fixture
names (carried by earlier patchsets of this change) are not worth their
complexity: hand-tuned fixture categories moved the expected slowest
android_browsertests shard by ~7 s and even a per-test duration table by

[remoting] Pass terminal_id separately in SetAgentStatus Mojo IPC

Moves TerminalControl into a dedicated remoting/proto/terminal.proto
file and updates ChromotingSessionServices::SetAgentStatus to accept
terminal_id as a separate parameter rather than embedding it in
mojom::AgentStatus. This prepares for migrating terminal remoting to
per-terminal WebRTC data channels where per-message terminal_id fields
are removed from TerminalControl submessages.

Because the mojo implementation is tightly-coupled to the proto
definition, this necessitates a change to the former unless we're
willing to keep an unused field in the latter. Since the full CL is
quite large, this one isolates only those changes required to update the
mojo interface. Nothing changes in terms of the trust relationship
between the sender and receiver--only the payload.

NO_IFTTT=TerminalControl.AgentInfo is extracted to terminal.proto in this CL and terminal_id is removed from it in the child CL.

[OpenInApp] Launch replacement NTP when closing last regular tab

When clicking "Open in app" on the last remaining tab in a regular
browser window, launch a replacement NTP via
TabCreatorUtil.launchNtp() before closing the tab. This matches WebAPK
install reparenting (WebApkReparentingHandler) and Desktop Chrome
(ReparentWebContentsIntoAppBrowser), keeping the browser window alive
instead of closing the window. Also guard the posted closeTab runnable
against tabs that are already closing or destroyed, and remove the
now-unused TabClosingSource.OPEN_IN_APP enum value.

[perf] Defer Dispatcher hooks until PoissonAllocationSampler starts

Allocator Dispatcher hooks (AllocatorShim and PartitionAlloc observers)
are installed at startup in every process, although
PoissonAllocationSampler only samples after a SamplesObserver is added.
Defer connecting them until then to avoid per-allocation dispatch
overhead while heap profiling is inactive.

Speedometer3 on M1 (Pinpoint, 150 runs; p < 0.01, no regressions):
  Score                                       +0.3%
  TodoMVC-jQuery                              -0.9%
  TodoMVC-JavaScript-ES5                      -0.8%
  TodoMVC-JavaScript-ES6-Webpack-Complex-DOM  -0.7%
  React-Stockcharts-SVG                       -0.4%

[Omnibox] Skip no-op TextView.setText when rebinding suggestion text

TextView.setText never short-circuits identical content: every call
copies the Spannable into a new SpannedString and, because line_1 and
line_2 are match_parent, synchronously rebuilds the layout. The
suggestion list is currently rebuilt wholesale several times per
keystroke, so most of these binds re-apply text the view already shows.
PropertyModel's own equality check does not help here because each
update creates fresh models and the RecyclerView rebinds recycled views
to them.

SuggestionViewViewBinder now compares the incoming SuggestionSpannable
against the text the TextView already holds (its own SpannedString
copy) via the new SuggestionSpannable.contentEquals, and skips setText
when both have the same text and visual spans. Nothing is cached, so
the check cannot go stale. Visibility and min-height handling are
unchanged.

SuggestionSpannable.equals is refactored on top of contentEquals. It
compares ImageSpans (used by TabGroupSuggestionProcessor, which renders
through this binder) by alignment and drawable identity, and no longer
asserts on unknown span types; it reports them as different, which only
costs an unnecessary setText. Tests pin that spans of equal count and
type but different extents are never considered equal, and that a
SpannedString copy compares equal to its source.

Measured on a Pixel 6 x86_64 emulator (API 35) with a scripted typing
scenario (6 queries x 2 repeats, 600 ms per key): 47% of text binds were
identical to the current contents, and total main-thread time in
setText for suggestion rows dropped from 1,152 ms to 716 ms (-38%),
with per-call cost unchanged. Those numbers were taken with an earlier
revision of this change that cached the last bound spannable instead of
reading it back from the TextView; the skip decision is identical and
the per-check cost differs only by a getText() call, so they were not
re-measured. Details in the bug.

Choice Engine: Clean up WipeChoicePrefsOnMissingDefaultSearchEngine flag

The `kWipeChoicePrefsOnMissingDefaultSearchEngine` feature has been
launched and enabled by default. This CL removes the feature flag and
makes the behavior permanent: if search engine choice metadata is
present but the default search engine pref is missing, the choice prefs
are wiped so that the user is prompted to choose again.

Also removes the `Search.ChoicePrefsCheck.WipeOnMissingDse` histogram,
which only recorded whether the feature was enabled. These wipes are
still recorded by `Search.ChoiceWipeReason`, in the "Missing default
search engine" bucket.

remoting: Fix frame timestamp and duration in WebrtcVideoEncoderVpx

SetCommonCodecParameters() configures config->g_timebase to milliseconds
(1 / 1000 s), matching WebrtcVideoEncoderAV1. However,
WebrtcVideoEncoderVpx::Encode() previously passed pts = 0 and
params.duration.InMicroseconds() to vpx_codec_encode(). Inside libvpx,
a duration of 33333 in a millisecond timebase was interpreted as 33.333
seconds per frame (0.03 FPS), and pts = 0 caused adjust_frame_rate() to
reset cpi->framerate to 0.03 FPS on every frame, inflating
rc->avg_frame_bandwidth by 1000x.

This change accumulates a monotonically increasing artificial_timestamp_
as a base::TimeDelta (avoiding integer millisecond truncation drift) and
passes artificial_timestamp_.InMilliseconds() and
params.duration.InMilliseconds() to vpx_codec_encode().

[Actor] Avoid stopForeground when updating pinned notification

Currently, moving the foreground service pin to another task while
Chrome is in the background throws
ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException. The swap calls
stopForeground() first, which resets the background start allowance.

Call only startForeground() with the new ID, so the service stays in
the foreground and no new start check runs.

That call, like stopForeground(STOP_FOREGROUND_REMOVE), makes Android
cancel the old untagged notification asynchronously, so the unpinned
task's notification must be reposted. A repost under the same key can
be removed by that late cancel, or inherit FLAG_FOREGROUND_SERVICE and
FLAG_NO_CLEAR and become non-dismissible.

The repost therefore uses UNPINNED_NOTIFICATION_TAG. Android never
treats a tagged notification as a foreground service notification, and
the cancel does not touch it. The tag stays until the task is pinned
again.

[iOS] Re-enable testSelectPasswordActionInIncognito

Re-enable PasswordViewControllerTestCase's
testSelectPasswordActionInIncognito, which was disabled in
crrev.com/c/5926293.

Fix three timing issues in the test and suite setup:
1. When the Keyboard Accessory Upgrade feature is enabled on iPhone,
   OpenPasswordManualFillView can tap the autofill form suggestion
   button slightly before the keyboard accessory chips finish animating
   into place. Wait for the button to appear via
   waitForUIElementToAppearWithMatcher: before tapping it.
2. Each test relaunches the app and starts loading the login page in
   -[PasswordViewControllerTestCase setUp] without waiting for the
   startup New Tab Page load to finish, which can occasionally stall the
   initial navigation on the New Tab Page on iPad and cause
   -[ChromeEarlGrey loadURL:] to fail waiting for the WebState to become
   visible. Call [ChromeEarlGrey waitForPageToFinishLoading] in -setUp
   before loading the login page.
3. -[PasswordViewControllerTestCase openOtherPasswords] taps the
   confirmation action sheet item without waiting for the modal "Other
   Passwords" view controller to finish presenting, which can race with
   the immediate visibility assertion. Wait for
   OtherPasswordsDismissMatcher() to appear before asserting
   visibility.

This CL fixes an existing test, so no new test is added. Verified
locally with
PasswordViewControllerTestCase/testSelectPasswordActionInIncognito:
- iPad Pro 11-inch (M5) (iOS 27.0): 3/3
- iPad Pro 11-inch (M5) (iOS 26.5): 3/3
- iPhone 17 Pro Max (iOS 27.0): 3/3
- iPhone 17 Pro Max (iOS 26.5): 3/3

[UndoTabClosures] Read pinned/extra data from the closed tab when saving closures

When several tabs are closed together, TabRestoreService asks the close
wrapper for each tab's pinned state and extra data by its index within
the closure. AndroidLiveTabContextCloseWrapper did not override
IsTabPinned/GetExtraDataForTab, so the base class looked up that index
in the live tab model and could read a different tab (e.g. a closed
unpinned tab was saved as pinned).

Behind kUndoableTabClosureRework, read both from the closed tab itself,
and also record the closed tab's id in the entry's extra data
(kUndoOldTabIdKey) so a later undo restore can map restored tabs back to
their original positions. Recent Tabs ignores the new key. Behavior is
unchanged with the flag off.

Single-tab closures are not affected by this change.

[Extensions] Restrict tab messaging receivers to extension processes

When an extension calls `chrome.tabs.sendMessage()` or
`chrome.tabs.connect()`, the browser registers frames in the tab as
receivers of the channel (`ExtensionMessagePort::RegisterFrame()`)
without checking whether each frame's process may act for the
extension. Without a `frameId`, that is every live frame in the tab. So
a cross-site subframe process that never ran the extension's content
script is still sent `DispatchOnConnect()`, gets the opener's messages,
and gets a `mojom::MessagePortHost` that lets it reply as if it were the
content script. Only the renderer filters these frames out, so a
compromised renderer can read and forge the extension's tab messages.

After this change, when the new
`kRestrictMessagingReceiverFramesToExtensionProcesses` feature is
enabled, the browser only registers a frame as a receiver if its
process is in `ProcessMap` for the extension, or has run a content
script or user script from the extension. This matches the checks the
browser already does when a renderer opens a channel to an extension.
Frames in other processes no longer get `DispatchOnConnect()` or the
channel's messages. The feature is disabled by default for now: with it
enabled, a Chrome App's messages no longer reach the app's own
webview-accessible resources shown in a `<webview>` (unless the app has
injected script into that `<webview>`), and that needs to be fixed
before the feature is enabled by default.

`ExtensionMessagePort::RegisterFrame()` now checks the frame's process
with a new helper, `CanProcessReceiveMessagesForExtension()`, which uses
`ProcessMap::Contains()`,
`ScriptInjectionTracker::DidProcessRunContentScriptFromExtension()` and
`ScriptInjectionTracker::DidProcessRunUserScriptFromExtension()`. This
covers tab-wide messages, messages to a specific `frameId` or
`documentId`, and `CreateForExtension()`.

The new browser test
`TabWideMessagingTest.SendMessageRegistrationOfNonContentScriptProcess`
runs with the feature enabled and disabled. It replaces the `b.com`
subframe's `mojom::LocalFrame` remote with an interceptor, using the
new `ExtensionWebContentsObserver::SetLocalFrameForTesting()` hook, and
checks whether the subframe gets `DispatchOnConnect()`. With the
feature enabled, it also checks that the subframe is registered once
`ScriptInjectionTracker` reports that its process ran the content
script.

[ChromeDriver] Add androidGrantPermissions capability

On Android, ChromeDriver clears the app data with `pm clear` before
launching (unless androidKeepAppDataDir is set). That also resets
runtime permission grants, and ChromeDriver then grants back only
android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS. On Android 17, reaching
RFC1918 addresses needs the runtime permission
android.permission.ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK, so every session loses it
and navigations to a LAN test server fail with
ERR_LOCAL_NETWORK_PERMISSION_MISSING. Android releases keep
promoting capabilities to runtime permissions, so rather than
extending a hardcoded list, this CL introduces a capability that
lets users choose what to grant.

Add goog:chromeOptions.androidGrantPermissions, a list of runtime
permissions to grant to androidPackage before launch:
- When absent, ChromeDriver grants the current default,
  POST_NOTIFICATIONS, and ignores failures, as before.
- When set, the list replaces the default ([] grants nothing) and
  any failed grant fails session creation with the `pm grant`
  output.
- Short names without a '.' expand to android.permission.<NAME>;
  other names are used as given.
- Each name must match [A-Za-z0-9_.]+, since it is passed to
  `adb shell pm grant`.

This also drops the stoi() parse of ro.build.version.release that
gated the old grant on Android 13+.

R=sadym@chromium.org

captive_portal: Show the standard SSL interstitial in portal windows

Captive portals often serve their login page over HTTPS with a
certificate that does not validate. In a dedicated sign-in window,
SSLErrorHandler can show CaptivePortalBlockingPage, which has no way to
proceed, and whose only action (open a login tab) is a no-op when there
is no browser, as in the ChromeOS sign-in and lock screen dialogs. The
user cannot sign in to the network.

SSLErrorHandler already avoids this for login tabs via
CaptivePortalTabHelper::IsLoginTab(). That bit is cleared once a probe
stops reporting a portal, which is right for a tab that returns to
normal browsing, but a sign-in window never does. Also treat
is_captive_portal_window() as a login surface. It is set once at
creation, and is already how captive portal secure DNS suppression is
gated.

Behavior changes only for kPopup surfaces: the ChromeOS sign-in and
lock screen dialogs, NetworkPortalSigninWindow (OTR profile), and the
desktop secure DNS popup. The last runs on the regular profile, where
proceeding records a certificate exception; it already shows the
overridable interstitial today, and now keeps doing so after a probe
clears IsLoginTab().

SSLBlockingPage::IsOverridable() still applies, so fatal errors and HSTS
hosts remain non-bypassable.

Tests cover a portal window after the login-tab bit is cleared and a
WebContents not hosted in a tab. Both fail without the
ssl_error_handler.cc change.

[Omnibox] Extract speech recognition intent creation and launch

Split the system speech recognizer flow in
VoiceRecognitionIntentHandler into dedicated steps:
- createSystemSpeechRecognitionIntent() builds the intent;
- launchRecognitionIntent() records the start event, shows the intent,
  and handles launch failure.

The start event is now recorded once by the launch step instead of
inside showSpeechRecognitionIntent(). This prepares for an additional
recognizer that may fall back to the system one, which must not record
the start event twice.

No behavior change.

[policy] Increase cloud policy cache size limit to 2 MB

Increase the maximum allowed user and machine (CBCM/CEC) cloud policy
cache file size from 1 MB to 2 MB.

M156 enterprise policy proto expansions (including large
ExtensionSettings bundles) can push user and machine cloud policy cache
files past the 1 MB kPolicySizeLimit. When this occurs,
base::ReadFileToStringWithMaxSize fails with LOAD_RESULT_LOAD_ERROR on
browser restart, discarding the cached policy and DM token.

This change introduces an enabled-by-default feature kill-switch,
kUserPolicyCacheSizeLimit2MB, which raises the disk read cache limit to
2 MB. In addition, DesktopCloudPolicyStore records the cache file size
in Enterprise.CloudPolicy.LocalCacheSize.User and
Enterprise.CloudPolicy.LocalCacheSize.Machine in kilobytes on startup.

UserCloudPolicyStoreTest.LoadPolicyExceedingOneMegabyte fails without
the fix and passes with it. Reverting the fix reproduces the failure,
and 20 repeat runs and related unit tests pass.

The tests and the fix were written with AI assistance.

Move WebContentsOcclusionCheckerMac out of content/app_shim_remote_cocoa
into components/remote_cocoa/app_shim as WindowOcclusionCheckerMac, with
no behavioral changes.

To decouple the checker from //content without changing its pull-based
update logic in this move CL, +[WebContentsViewCocoa initialize]
supplies the two //content predicates (-[NSWindow
containsWebContentsViewCocoa] and !browser->IsShuttingDown()) via
+[WindowOcclusionCheckerMac
setWindowPredicate:canPerformUpdatesPredicate:]. A follow-up CL replaces
this seam with reference-counted window tracking so pure-Views top-level
windows can participate.

The move was suggested by kerenzhu@.

parent
57d989fd5045a0544ec7e73a18d4664c4ff27320 [ diff ] 
[SafetyHub] Fix abusive notification permissions state inconsistency

When a user manually re-grants ALLOW for a notification that was
previously revoked for abusive behavior (e.g.
SocialEngineeringBlocklist), the revocation entry should be marked as
'ignore'. Previously, this was only done for suspicious content
auto-revocation. This inconsistency led to CHECK failures during
background checks because the origin had an ALLOW setting but a 'revoke'
dict status.

This CL updates OnPermissionChanged to correctly set the entry to
'ignore' for all abusive notification revocation sources when the
setting is changed to ALLOW. It also removes the CHECK in
ShouldCheckOrigin and returns false instead, which gracefully skips
checking these origins, preventing crashes for existing profiles that
may already have the inconsistent state.

parent
bcaea8aa011163373407cda07b952ac70051ddc7 [ diff ] 
[ttc] Add mic mute to the TTC session

Lets the session UI pause the microphone, for the large-screen voice
plate's pause button.

- Conversation::SetMicMuted() stops and restarts the AudioController's
  capture, which is where the mute state lives: IsMicMuted() asks it.
- AudioController::StopCapture() now drops audio captured before it that
  hasn't been delivered yet, so none of it reaches the model, and tells
  observers (OnCaptureStopped()), so the level settles at 0.
- SessionControllerImpl::SetMicMuted() carries it out (journaled) and
  returns whether the state changed; IsMicMuted() reads it from the
  conversation. Both only apply while the session is live, since capture
  only starts then.
- TtcKeyedService gains SetMicMuted() / IsMicMuted(), which forward to
  its SessionControllerImpl and which the Android bridge calls.
- On Android, TtcKeyedService.setMicMuted() / isMicMuted() call through
  to it, and setMicMuted() tells the Java observers when the state
  changed (Observer#onMicMutedChanged()), so that every window's UI
  stays in sync.

Remove server-synthesized Omnibox histograms from Chromium XML

Remove six Omnibox histograms (`Omnibox.InputType`,
`Omnibox.IsPasteAndGo`, `Omnibox.JustDeletedText`,
`Omnibox.NumTypedTerms`, `Omnibox.SuggestionUsed.OfferedTabMatch`,
and `Omnibox.SuggestionUsed.SelectedTabMatch`) along with their
unused enums (`BooleanOffered` and `OmniboxInputType`).

These histograms are synthesized server-side from `OmniboxEvent`
proto fields rather than logged by the Chromium client, and their
definitions have been moved to the internal server-side histogram
configuration so they can be tagged as synthetic metrics.

This fixes the cross-origin check for relatedTarget for both of the
fixes in commit bb79a99bd4473e26031cd5433e34d047fa527f3c to handle null
execution context better (by treating it as cross-origin).

than setting relatedTarget to null, since I think that's more
appropriate for a defense-in-depth check (and if we're actually
hitting it we may need to fix the callers that are causing it in other
ways).

a5df31f839191104ff3339cec1c99c7e52a4a871 [ diff ] 
[ReadAloud] Drive MediaSession state from utility playback states

Previously, ReadAloudService::Pause() synchronously notified
ReadAloudPlaybackSession and the UI delegate of kPaused, while
ReadAloudService::OnPlaybackStateChanged() did not forward utility state
changes (kPlaying, kPaused, kEndOfStream) to ReadAloudPlaybackSession.
As a result, utility-initiated pauses (such as play-on-ready timeouts or
end-of-stream) never updated MediaSession.

Update ReadAloudService and ReadAloudPlaybackSession so utility playback
states drive MediaSession:

- Remove the synchronous NotifyPlaybackPaused() and
  NotifyPlaybackStateChanged(kPaused) calls from ReadAloudService::Pause()
  so the utility's kPaused report drives both MediaSession and the UI
  delegate.
- Call media_session_->NotifyPlaybackPaused() on kPaused and
  kEndOfStream in OnPlaybackStateChanged(), keeping Read Aloud in the
  MediaSession as a paused player at end of stream so resuming from the
  media notification routes Play() back to Read Aloud.
- Call media_session_->NotifyPlaybackStarted() on kPlaying in
  OnPlaybackStateChanged().
- Unconditionally clear pending_session_command_ via std::exchange() in
  ReadAloudPlaybackSession::ConsumePendingSessionCommand() so an
  unanswered session suspend or resume cannot remain stale across a
  subsequent transition.

Declare PrerenderHostRegistry as a stateful MemoryConsumer

With kStatefulMemoryPressure enabled, PrerenderHostRegistry maintains a
lasting limit: new triggers are capped by the scaled limit and
OnReleaseMemory() only evicts down to it, so repeated calls have no
effect. When the feature is disabled, the memory coordinator policy
treats all consumers as stateless regardless of their traits, so the
legacy path is unchanged.

Fix null dereference in validation overlay teardown after adoption

BlockingFocusWithoutUserActivation can prevent reportValidity() from
focusing an invalid input while still allowing its validation bubble to
be shown. Removing the unfocused input starts the 133 ms hide animation
instead of destroying the overlay through focus-change cleanup.

If the input's subtree is adopted into a detached document, the anchor's
document changes while the overlay remains attached to the original
page. DocumentDetached() previously checked only the anchor's current
document, so teardown of the original document missed the pending
overlay. An immediate reload could then clear the host frame's view
before Page::WillBeDestroyed() reset the validation client.
FrameOverlay::Destroy() dereferenced the null view when requesting
repaint.

Also destroy the validation message when the document hosting its
overlay detaches. Use the overlay's existing frame to identify that
document, ensuring cleanup happens before its view is cleared without
introducing another document reference. Preserve the existing
anchor-document cleanup and normal animated hiding. The focus policy and
its shipping default are unchanged.

Add a regression with a sandboxed iframe, an invalid email input, and
adoption into a detached XML document followed by frame teardown.
Explicitly enable BlockingFocusWithoutUserActivation and run outside
web-test mode so neither a disabled shipping default nor test-only
immediate hiding can mask the bug. Supply a custom validation message
because the unit-test platform has no localized validation strings.

With the final test unchanged, fresh Windows builds reproduce the
original crash in all three paint configurations without the production
fix and pass all three with it.

Rework PrerenderHostRegistryTest to not set `load_flags` directly.

`load_flags` can be calculated from information the browser knows, so
we should remove them from BeginNavigationParams. This is a small step
in that direction.

This CL also removes the capability of the NavigationSimulatorImpl of
setting load_flags (which was only used by the
PrerenderHostRegistryTest).

[CSS] Don't try the property grammar on values that start with var() or env()

CSSPropertyParser::ParseValueStart() first runs the longhand or
shorthand parser on a declaration's value and, if that fails, rewinds
the token stream (re-tokenizing the lookahead) and consumes it again
as an unparsed declaration with variable references. A value whose
first token is var( or env( can never succeed on the first path, since
no property grammar accepts these substitution functions, and such
values are a large fraction of the declarations in modern stylesheets
("color: var(--x)"). Check the first token and go straight to the
unparsed-declaration path for them. Other substitution functions
(attr(), if(), ...) are left alone since they are behind flags and
rarer. No behavior change; a new test checks that such values (long-
and shorthand, with !important, invalid ones) produce the same pending
substitution values as before.

Measured with blink_perf_tests (Linux x64 release, 30 runs,
compare_blink_perf) using the benchmark additions from
crrev.com/c/8360829 (StyleCalcPerfTest Parse16BitTime and
CSSParserPerfTest), which are not part of this chain:
on its own, at this point, this is within noise (CSSParserPerfTest
Utility EagerParseTime +0.1% [-0.5, +0.6], StyleCalcPerfTest ParseTime
-0.1% [-0.3, +0.2], Parse16BitTime -0.3%): the skipped attempt is a
small fixed cost per declaration next to tokenizing and the value
parsing that follows. It was previously measured at about +4% of eager
parse time on a large var()-heavy sheet on top of the tokenizer changes
in crrev.com/c/8262930's chain, which make the rest cheap enough for it
to show.

[Signin] Disallow PrimaryAccountMutator calls from OnPrimaryAccountChanged

Mutating the primary account while OnPrimaryAccountChanged()
notifications are being dispatched triggers nested notifications, and
observers that haven't been notified yet receive events that don't
match the current state.

- PrimaryAccountManager tracks whether OnPrimaryAccountChanged()
  notifications (to SigninClient and observers) are in progress.
- PrimaryAccountMutatorImpl CHECKs that none of its methods are called
  while these notifications are being dispatched.

[webapps] Add WebAppManager test seam and unit tests for TwaInstaller

Previously, TwaInstaller retrieved
android.content.pm.webapp.WebAppManager directly from the application
context via getSystemService() and had no unit test coverage in
components_junit_tests. This prevented unit tests and hermetic
instrumentation tests on emulators without the WebApp Mainline module
from injecting a test or mock WebAppManager instance.

This change adds TwaInstaller.setWebAppManagerForTesting() (registered
with ResettersForTesting) and adds TwaInstallerTest to
components_junit_tests covering WebAppInstallRequest construction,
install result callback forwarding to native (success, user
cancellation, and error), fallback handling when WebAppManager is null
or the manifest URL is empty or SDK < CINNAMON_BUN, and
TwaInstaller.isInstalled() query handling.

[Omnibox] Add 4dp top padding to suggestions in narrow tablet windows

In a narrow (<600dp wide) window on a tablet, the suggestions dropdown
had no top padding, so the first suggestion sat flush against the bottom
of the toolbar / focused Omnibox.

omnibox_suggestion_list_padding_top is 8dp only under
values-sw600dp-w600dp (wide tablet windows) and 0dp in values/ (phones,
where the Omnibox and suggestions form a continuous surface). Narrow
tablet windows match neither override and fell back to 0dp.

Define the dimen as 4dp in values-sw600dp so narrow tablet windows get
the requested spacing. The more specific -w600dp qualifier still applies
in wide windows, and phones are unaffected.

[FindInPage] Add support to jump outside viewport

When searching pages with dense or repeated text (such as logs, tables,
or navigation headers), cycling through every visible match inside the
current viewport with Find in Page is slow and repetitive.

This change adds support (guarded behind `kFindInPageSkipViewport`,
disabled by default) to skip matches visible in the current viewport and
jump directly to the next or previous match outside the viewport,
falling back to the adjacent match when all matches are visible.

Users can trigger this via the new "Previous outside view" and "Next
outside view" buttons in the Find bar, or with Alt+Enter /
Shift+Alt+Enter (Ctrl+Enter is already used to activate a matched link).

Screenshots:
- https://storage.cloud.google.com/chromium-translation-screenshots/69aeb11ac3ecfbb1864c726b766b286be301c806
- https://storage.cloud.google.com/chromium-translation-screenshots/6483167b334bcc0f721dda7ca1c4824b5a4ad227

android_deps: Skip remote POM and HEAD checks for ignored deps

Every setupRepository run fetched the POM and sent a HEAD request for
all resolved deps, including subproject, excluded, and EXISTING_LIBS
deps whose metadata is never written. Populate DependencyDescription
entries and exclude flags first, then skip remote POM and HEAD requests
for deps ignored by BuildConfigGenerator.ignoreForCurrentProject (saves
~590 HTTP requests on android_deps, including all androidx.dev requests,
and cuts POM parsing from ~9s to ~1s with identical outputs).

[Vertical Tabs] Fix autoscroll on tab group context menus on short windows

<After>
https://screencast.googleplex.com/cast/NTcxMDkwMzYwODYwNjcyMHxkYzY1OWQwNy1jYg

<Root Cause>
This issue only happens for tab group context menus.
1) The tab group context menu (tab_strip_group_menu_layout.xml) has an
outermost ScrollView, and inside it, the group name text box and color picker sit above the ListView (tab_group_action_menu_list).
2) Note that for regular context menus, tab_group_action_menu_list is the only thing in mContentView.
3) When TabOverflowMenuHolder#show() focuses tab_group_action_menu_list,
Android's outer ScrollView sees that the focused view is down at the bottom, so when the window is short, the ScrollView automatically scrolls down to bring that ListView into view.

<Fix>
For vertical tabs, configure the outer ScrollView (mContentView) with
focusableInTouchMode = true and FOCUS_BEFORE_DESCENDANTS so that TabOverflowMenuHolder#show() focuses the ScrollView itself at the top
instead of scrolling down to the ListView or highlighting the group title EditText.

Reland "Fix sandbox initialization for OnDeviceModelExecution on Linux"

This is a reland of commit 28871b4af455d4dc4446ccc5aa764a950e074c82

The original CL (https://crrev.com/c/8387676) made Seccomp-BPF engage in
the on-device model process (previously skipped due to driver threads
[1]), and was reverted (https://crrev.com/c/8423698) after failing on
optimization_guide-linux.

Changes relative to the original CL:

1. In on_device_model::PreSandboxHook(), call PreSandboxInit() before
   content::LoadLibrariesForGpu(), and pin "libvulkan.so.1" with
   dlopen("libvulkan.so.1", RTLD_NOW | RTLD_NOLOAD | RTLD_NODELETE)
   while Dawn's warm-up `instance` is in scope. In the original CL,
   LoadLibrariesForGpu()'s bare dlopen("libvulkan.so.1") [2] ran first
   and loaded the system Vulkan loader (non-component builds), and Dawn
   then dlopen()ed "<module_dir>/libvulkan.so.1" (search order: module
   dir, executable dir, bare name [3]) as a second copy, leaving only
   SwiftShader discoverable. Calling PreSandboxInit() first lets Dawn
   load its preferred loader, and pinning it by SONAME prevents Dawn's
   DynamicLib destructor from dlclose()ing it when `instance` is
   destroyed [4], so LoadLibrariesForGpu() and ChromeML reuse it.

2. In on_device_model::PreSandboxHook(), grant broker permissions for
   /dev/dri/renderD* (read-write), /sys/dev/char/<major>:<minor>/
   (recursive read-only), and /usr/share/libdrm/amdgpu.ids (read-only).
   With Seccomp-BPF active, file opens go through the broker, and on
   non-ChromeOS Linux content::FilePermissionsForGpu() only grants
   /dev/dri/card0..9 and /dev/nvidia* (AddDrmGpuPermissions() and
   AddAmdGpuPermissions() are ChromeOS-only) [5]. When ChromeML creates
   a Vulkan device after sandbox engagement, Mesa drivers (Intel ANV
   anv_CreateDevice(), AMD RADV) open /dev/dri/renderD* read-write,
   libdrm reads /sys/dev/char/<major>:<minor>/, and libdrm_amdgpu reads
   /usr/share/libdrm/amdgpu.ids.

3. In GpuProcessPolicy::EvaluateSyscall() (used on non-ChromeOS Linux
   [6]), allow sched_setscheduler() with non-realtime policies
   (SCHED_OTHER, SCHED_BATCH, SCHED_IDLE) on any thread. Previously, it
   fell through to RestrictSchedTarget(GetPolicyPid(), sysno) [7], which
   only allows targeting the calling thread or GetPolicyPid() and
   crashed with SIGSYS [8] when Mesa's util_queue called
   pthread_setschedparam(thread, SCHED_BATCH, ...) on shader-compiler
   worker threads during vkCreateComputePipelines(). Realtime policies
   remain restricted by RestrictSchedTarget().

4. In UtilityMain(), set the default
   sandbox_options.use_amd_specific_policies from
   ShouldUseAmdGpuPolicy() before the per-sandbox switch instead of
   after [9], where it overwrote the value set by
   on_device_model::AddSandboxLinuxOptions() on AMD GPUs [10] (used on
   ChromeOS/Chromecast for seccomp policy, broker permissions, and
   library preloads [5, 6]).

[1] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:sandbox/policy/linux/sandbox_linux.cc;l=369-408;drc=dc4601072eecf55ca3f1ee0b211fc4486b20afed
[2] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:content/common/gpu_pre_sandbox_hook_linux.cc;l=585-593;drc=dc4601072eecf55ca3f1ee0b211fc4486b20afed

[6] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:sandbox/policy/linux/sandbox_seccomp_bpf_linux.cc;l=124-147;drc=dc4601072eecf55ca3f1ee0b211fc4486b20afed
[7] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:sandbox/linux/seccomp-bpf-helpers/baseline_policy.cc;l=234-237;drc=dc4601072eecf55ca3f1ee0b211fc4486b20afed
[8] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:sandbox/linux/seccomp-bpf-helpers/syscall_parameters_restrictions.cc;l=398-421;drc=dc4601072eecf55ca3f1ee0b211fc4486b20afed
[9] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:content/utility/utility_main.cc;l=405-411;drc=dc4601072eecf55ca3f1ee0b211fc4486b20afed
[10] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:content/utility/on_device_model/on_device_model_sandbox_init.cc;l=50-53;drc=dc4601072eecf55ca3f1ee0b211fc4486b20afed

Original change's description:
> Fix sandbox initialization for OnDeviceModelExecution on Linux
>
> On Linux and ChromeOS, driver warming in on_device_model::PreSandboxInit
> spawns background driver threads. Previously, PreSandboxInit was called
> in UtilityMain before sandbox initialization. This created threads
> before SandboxLinux::StartBrokerProcess called fork(), which is unsafe
> in a multi-threaded process. Additionally, the spawned threads caused
> InitializeSandbox to fail to engage Seccomp-BPF.
>
> This CL fixes the issues by:
>
> 1. Deferring PreSandboxInit on Linux/ChromeOS into PreSandboxHook,
>    executing it immediately after StartBrokerProcess has safely forked
>    the broker while the process is strictly single-threaded.
> 2. Setting allow_threads_during_sandbox_init = true and
>    check_for_open_directories = false in AddSandboxLinuxOptions,
>    allowing StartSeccompBPF to apply the filter across all driver
>    threads via TSYNC.
> 3. Adding checks in RunOnDeviceModel to ensure PreSandboxInit was
>    called and that Seccomp-BPF is active on supported kernels.
> 4. Re-enabling the seccomp_bpf_started verification for
>    Sandbox::kOnDeviceModelExecution in
>    UtilityProcessSandboxBrowserTest.
>

[CSS] Report 16-bit parse time in the style perf tests

A stylesheet decodes to a 16-bit string as soon as it contains a single
non-Latin-1 character (an ellipsis or an arrow in a content: value is
enough), which is common for large real-world sheets, and the
tokenizer's fast paths currently only apply to 8-bit strings. Nothing
in blink_perf_tests measures that today.

Make StyleCalcPerfTest additionally parse each dumped page's sheets as
16-bit strings and report BlinkStyleParse16BitTime next to
BlinkStyleParseTime; compare_blink_perf labels it "Parse, 16-bit".

Test-only; no behavior change.

[iOS] Consolidate FRE Android switcher promo variation flags

Unify the standalone FRE device switcher signal flags with the Android
switcher promo flag so that signal evaluation and promo presentation are
controlled by a single variation rather than separate post-FRE checks.

Removing the FRE-completion signal queries and duplicate SwitcherInfo
histograms prepares for evaluating both signals at promo presentation
time and comparing them in shared UMA histograms.

OBSOLETE_HISTOGRAM[IOS.FirstRun.DefaultBrowserPromo.SwitcherInfoResult]=Replaced
by IOS.FirstRun.DefaultBrowserPromo.SegmentationResult
OBSOLETE_HISTOGRAM[IOS.FirstRun.DefaultBrowserPromo.SwitcherInfoLatency.Success]=Replaced
by IOS.FirstRun.DefaultBrowserPromo.SegmentationLatency.Success
OBSOLETE_HISTOGRAM[IOS.FirstRun.DefaultBrowserPromo.SwitcherInfoLatency.Failure]=Replaced
by IOS.FirstRun.DefaultBrowserPromo.SegmentationLatency.Failure

[iOS] Re-enable HistorySystemTestCase.testSearchSyncedHistory

testSearchSyncedHistory was disabled on iOS 26+ in crrev.com/c/6832155
and suppressed on simulators and iPad devices in crrev.com/c/8249702,
so it has not run on any current CQ simulator (iOS 26.5 and 27.0).

History search results are fetched asynchronously from the history
service, which EarlGrey does not synchronize with, so the checks that
the synced entry is shown and that the other entries are filtered out
could run before the table view was updated. Wait for the other entries
to be filtered out, then for the synced entry to be shown: the synced
entry is also in the unfiltered list, so checking it first would not
prove that the filter ran. Remove the iOS 26+ early return and the
test_expectations.txt suppressions.

Tested locally (3/3 passes per simulator on iPhone 16 Pro and iPad A16
across iOS 26.5 and 27.0, plus the enabled HistorySystemTestCase suite;
not verified on a physical iPad device).

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

parent
698f445ae6423d8b1bf25e0786a38a45ae52d1d7 [ diff ] 
[tools/perf] Add story diagnostic to LoadLine crossbench results

Unlike other Crossbench benchmarks in crossbench_result_converter.py,
_loadline() did not attach the 'stories' (reserved_infos.STORIES.name)
diagnostic to its output histograms.

As a result, LoadLine metrics were uploaded to Chromeperf as 4-part test
paths (Master/Bot/Benchmark/Metric) with unescaped_story_name = None,
causing Chromeperf's AlertGroupWorkflow to skip auto-triage bisection
and Sandwich verification for LoadLine regressions, and preventing
Pinpoint's ReadValue quest from matching metrics when a story is
expected.

Pass the story name (defaulting to 'default') to _loadline() and attach
it as a shared STORIES diagnostic on LoadLine histograms.

parent
8f889cf956d223cb16a9daf5fc098c158e46798a [ diff ] 
🌺 Detach root ChromeNativeWindowSurface in GLSurfaceEGLSurfaceControl::Destroy

On Android 14 (`chrome/ci/android-14-arm64-rel-tests`, Pixel 7 `panther`
running `AP2A.240705.004` `userdebug`), `SurfaceFlinger` periodically
aborts (`SIGABRT`) during `content_browsertests` teardown, triggering a
userspace soft-reboot (`Zygote` / `system_server` restart) that causes
dozens of subsequent tests on the shard to fail:

Builder:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chrome/builders/ci/android-14-arm64-rel-tests

Example failing builds:
- https://ci.chromium.org/b/8686217497885042001
- https://ci.chromium.org/b/8686220987279325937

Exact logcat crash sequence (identical across crashes):
```
10-24 22:08:21.657 26707 26707 I cr_NativeTest: test run finished with command line flags: --gtest_filter=All/NavigationRequestThrottleResultWithErrorPageBrowserTest.WillRedirectRequest/4 --single-process-tests ...
10-24 22:08:21.659 17907 17907 I Process : Sending signal. PID: 26707 SIG: 9
10-24 22:08:21.678   562   562 F SurfaceFlinger: Couldnt find layer object for RequestedLayerState{org.chromium.content_browsertests_apk/ChromeNativeWindowSurface#17307 parentId=17304 !handle}
10-24 22:08:21.678   562   562 F libc    : Fatal signal 6 (SIGABRT), code -1 (SI_QUEUE) in tid 562 (surfaceflinger), pid 562 (surfaceflinger)
  #02 __android_log_assert
  #03 android::SurfaceFlinger::commit(android::PhysicalDisplayId, ...)
  #04 android::scheduler::Scheduler::onFrameSignal(...)
```

Root Cause:
1. `GLSurfaceEGLSurfaceControl` creates `root_surface_`
   (`ChromeNativeWindowSurface`) as a child layer of the `ANativeWindow`
   (`parentId=17304`) via `ASurfaceControl_createFromWindow`, and
   creates `surface_list_` (`ChromeChildSurface`) as children of
   `root_surface_`.
2. In `GLSurfaceEGLSurfaceControl::Destroy()`, when
   `!preserve_children_` (such as during `ContentViewRenderView::Destroy`
   at browser test teardown), `transaction.SetParent(*surface.surface,
   nullptr)` detaches every `ChromeChildSurface` from `root_surface_`
   and calls `transaction.Apply()`, queueing a child-hierarchy update on
   `ChromeNativeWindowSurface` while it remains attached to
   `parentId=17304`.
3. Immediately after `transaction.Apply()`, `root_surface_.reset()`
   calls `ASurfaceControl_release()` on `ChromeNativeWindowSurface`
   without reparenting it to `nullptr`, dropping the client binder
   handle (`!handle`) while `ChromeNativeWindowSurface` is still
   parented to `17304` with a pending `RequestedLayerState`.
4. On the next VSync (`SurfaceFlinger::commit`), Android 14 `userdebug`
   hits `ALOG_ASSERT` (`Couldnt find layer object for
   RequestedLayerState{.../ChromeNativeWindowSurface#17307
   parentId=17304 !handle}`).

Fix:
Also reparent `*root_surface_` to `nullptr` in the teardown transaction
when `!preserve_children_` before `root_surface_.reset()` releases its
`ASurfaceControl` handle.

Re-enable testOpenGoogleServicesSettings, testCancelAllowChromeSignin,
and testAllowChromeSigninDisabledForSupervisedUsers in
GoogleServicesSettingsTestCase.

services settings moved to their own directory in crrev.com/c/7759674

marked FLAKY_ for follow-up investigation.

[APC] Expose explicit input-blocked and disabled reasons

When input is blocked on an element—from pointer-events: none, inert
subtrees, or disabled form controls—AIPageContentAgent previously
dropped all interaction metadata. Downstream callers could not tell why
a node was inactive, or had to rely on viewport signals that vanish
off-screen.

This CL reports explicit disabled reasons instead:
- Adds kPointerEventsNone and kVisuallyUnreachable to mojom and maps
  them to proto.
- Gathers disabled reasons in a post-geometry pass to evaluate visual
  reachability alongside other signals.
- Keeps disabled reasons on elements even when scrolled off-screen.

WebUI Toolbar: Fix HelpBubbleFactoryViewsBrowsertest

When WebUI Toolbar is enabled, the app menu button is hosted inside the
WebUI toolbar rather than as a native Views child in ToolbarView.
HelpBubbleFactoryViewsBrowsertest::GetAnchorElement() queried
ElementTrackerViews::GetFirstMatchingView() for
kToolbarAppMenuButtonElementId, which returned nullptr and crashed in
GetElementForView().

Because HelpBubbleFactoryViewsBrowsertest tests HelpBubbleFactoryViews
(which requires a native Views anchor), anchor the test help bubble to
ToolbarView instead. ToolbarView remains a Views view in both Views and
WebUI toolbar configurations, and its right edge repositions when the
browser window widens in GetAndUpdateBounds.

Fixed tests in HelpBubbleFactoryViewsBrowsertest:
* GetAndUpdateBounds
* GetContext
* InvokeUi_default
* ShowAndClose

[ContextualTasks] Record extension handshake and postMessage telemetry

Add UMA for the Contextual Tasks component extension's Service Worker
port handshake and search message exchange with the Search Web page
(background.ts, ContextualTasksExtensionServiceWorkerHandler, and
ContextualTasksWebContentsUserData):

 - ExtensionHandshake.Status: outcome per connection attempt (Success,
   Host origin rejected, Frame detached, Mojo request failed, Invalid
   document ID).
 - ExtensionHandshake.Latency: time from document connection until
   HandshakeResponse.
 - ExtensionPostMessage.Error: dropped messages, by reason (Untrusted
   origin, Unexpected data type, Message too large, Invalid document
   ID, Proto parse failed, Mojo pipe closed).
 - ExtensionPostMessage.QueuedSearchMessagesDropped: search messages
   still queued when a page navigates, reconnects, or tears down
   before the handshake completes, recorded once per connection
   including 0.

[WebUI Toolbar] Share drop simulation between toolbar drop tests

WebUIHomeControlTestBase and WebUIToolbarDropBrowserTest each had their
own copy of the code that replays the WebContentsViewAura drag-and-drop
sequence (FilterDropData, DragTargetDragEnter, PreHandleDragUpdate,
DragTargetDragOver, HandleOnPerformingDrop, DragTargetDrop) and builds
the link, text, link+text and file drop data.

This CL moves that logic into WebUIToolbarDropSimulator in
webui_test_utils.{h,cc}. Each fixture now owns a simulator, sets the
drop point for its control, and forwards its Simulate*Drop() helpers to
it. Test bodies are unchanged.

The shared PerformDrop() is the toolbar variant: when DragOver is
refused it sends DragLeave and returns false, and it supports
`drag_exited_before_drop`.

This prepares for WebUI omnibox drop tests that reuse the same
simulation.

No behavior change; test-only refactor.

[CSS] Don't rescan unparsed declaration values to strip trailing whitespace

CSSVariableParser::ConsumeUnparsedDeclaration() took the text between
the first token and the stream position after ConsumeUnparsedValue(),
and then ran StripTrailingWhitespaceAndComments() over it: a
character-by-character quote/comment state machine over the whole value
for 16-bit text (and for any 8-bit value containing a '/'). This runs
for every custom property and every declaration containing var(), i.e.
for a large share of the declarations in a modern sheet.

The tokens were just consumed, so the information is already there:
ConsumeUnparsedValue() now optionally reports the offset just past the
last non-whitespace token it consumed (comments are not tokens, so they
are excluded too), and ConsumeUnparsedDeclaration() uses that. The one
case that still needs looking at the text is a last token that itself
ends in whitespace (an unterminated string, url() or function running
into the end of the input), where trailing whitespace is stripped as
before while escaped whitespace, which is part of the token, is kept.
StripTrailingWhitespaceAndComments() stays for the CSSOM callers.

No behavior change intended; a new test pins the stored text for these
cases on 8- and 16-bit input.

Measured with blink_perf_tests (Linux x64 release, 30 runs,
compare_blink_perf) using the benchmark additions from
crrev.com/c/8360829 (StyleCalcPerfTest Parse16BitTime and
CSSParserPerfTest), which are not part of this chain:
CSSParserPerfTest Utility (16-bit ~1.4 MB utility-first sheet, most
declarations use var()) EagerParseTime +4.9% [+4.3, +5.5],
LazyParseAndPropertiesTime +4.6% [+4.3, +4.9]; Utility8Bit +2.7% /
+2.8%. LazyParseTime (declarations not parsed) +0.6%. StyleCalcPerfTest
ParseTime +0.5% [+0.2, +0.8], Parse16BitTime +1.1% [+0.8, +1.3] over
the nine pages. (Measured over this and the previous, perf-neutral, CL.)

[iOS] Re-enable `testShowSyncPassphraseInNewWindowAndDismiss`

Re-enable `testShowSyncPassphraseInNewWindowAndDismiss` in
`sync_encryption_passphrase_table_view_controller_egtest.mm`, which was
disabled in crrev.com/c/5383899 due to failures on iPad.

Two issues caused the test to fail in multi-window on iPad:
1. Calling `openNewWindow` and `waitUntilReadyWindowWithNumber:` does
   not guarantee that the identity error infobar or the presented
   `SyncEncryptionPassphraseTableViewController` has finished appearing,
   so immediately tapping the infobar enter button or the navigation bar
   cancel button raced with their presentation.
2. EarlGrey's `grey_tap()` fails on elements in the second window with
   an occlusion error because `GREYUIWindowProvider` composites windows
   across all `UIWindowScene`s at `{0, 0}`, causing window 0 and its
   `ScopedUIBlocker` overlay window to falsely obscure window 1 during
   the visibility check.

Fix this by waiting for both buttons to appear in window 1 via
`waitForUIElementToAppearWithMatcher:`, tapping them with
`TapAtOffsetOf` (which dispatches XCUITest taps in the target window),
and waiting for the cancel button to disappear via
`waitForUIElementToDisappearWithMatcher:` before closing window 1.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

[rust] Fix gnrt update/vendor after the ICU4X 2.4.0 update

Since crrev.com/c/8633019, `gnrt update` and `gnrt vendor` fail on a
clean checkout with "failed to select a version for `icu_properties`".
Every third-party Rust crate roll runs these commands, so no crate can
be rolled until this is fixed.

Why they fail:
- chromium_crates_io/Cargo.toml now requires icu_properties ^2.4.0.
- harfrust 0.14.0, as published on crates.io, requires exactly
  icu_properties 2.2.0.
- crrev.com/c/8633019 relaxed that requirement with a local patch to
  Chromium's vendored copy of harfrust. Builds and `gnrt gen` read the
  vendored copy, so they work. `gnrt update` and `gnrt vendor` read the
  crates.io version, which still has the exact pin, so Cargo cannot
  pick an icu_properties version.

Repro on origin/main ba3a1adcba90f:
  $ tools/crates/run_gnrt.py update -- smallvec@1.16.2
  error: failed to select a version for `icu_properties`.
      ... required by package `harfrust v0.14.0`
  versions that meet the requirements `=2.2.0` are: 2.2.0
    previously selected package `icu_properties v2.4.0`
  cargo update exited with status exit status: 101
With this CL the same command updates smallvec 1.16.2 -> 1.16.3.

Fix: a [patch.crates-io] entry tells Cargo to use the vendored,
already-patched harfrust instead of the crates.io one. No code changes:
Cargo.lock only drops harfrust's crates.io source line, and `gnrt gen`
produces no BUILD.gn changes.

While the [patch.crates-io] entry exists, Cargo will not update
harfrust automatically. Remove the entry once harfrust publishes a
release without the exact icu_properties pin.

Prepared with AI assistance.

[Password Manager] Use UTF-16 in presenter revoke

In PasswordManagerUIHandler::RevokeActorLoginPermission, the
deserialized ActorLoginPermission already stores a UTF-16 username from
Mojo StructTraits, and
SavedPasswordsPresenter::RevokeActorLoginPermission compares that
username against StoredCredential::username_value, which is also UTF-16.
Previously, SavedPasswordsPresenter accepted a UTF-8 std::string,
forcing a redundant UTF-16 -> UTF-8 -> UTF-16 conversion between the UI
handler and presenter.

This change updates SavedPasswordsPresenter::RevokeActorLoginPermission
to accept std::string_view for signon_realm and std::u16string_view for
username, eliminating the redundant string conversions in
PasswordManagerUIHandler and SavedPasswordsPresenterTest.

WebUIPinnedToolbarActions is enabled:

  pinned toolbar button registers asynchronously with ElementTracker
  after its slide-in animation completes.

  NamedWidgetShownWaiter in
  ExclusiveAccessBubbleShownForTabFullscreenDownloadThenPartialView with
  WaitForShow(kToolbarDownloadBubbleElementId) so the UI thread
  processes the asynchronous WebUI anchor bounds IPC needed to show the
  download bubble.
- MediaRouterUIInteractiveUITest: In OpenDialogWithMediaRouterAction,
  after the page reload closes the Cast dialog and unhighlights the
  toolbar button, wait for views::kMinimumTimeBetweenButtonClicks
  (100ms) before clicking the button again so HighlightTracker does not
  suppress the click.
- InteractionTestUtilSimulatorWebUI::PressButton: When simulating a
  pointer press on a TrackedElementWebUI, close any active
  close-on-deactivate BubbleDialogDelegate anchored to the element with
  ClosedReason::kLostFocus after dispatching ClickElement, matching the
  native focus-loss deactivation that a real pointer press on the WebUI
  surface causes (fixing EphemeralToolbarIconForDialog).

[iOS] Fix iframe element bounds and re-enable manual fill iframe test

Re-enable PasswordViewControllerTestCase's
testPasswordControllerSupportsIFrameMessaging, which was disabled in
crrev.com/c/7878653 for failing on iPad.

TapWebElementWithIdInFrame calls web::test::GetBoundingRectOfElement
(ios/web/public/test/web_view_interaction_test_util.mm) to compute the
tap point in the web view. Previously, kGetBoundsScript returned
element.getBoundingClientRect() directly, whose left and top coordinates
are relative to the iframe's own viewport rather than the top-level
document viewport, causing taps on elements inside an iframe to miss
whenever the iframe was not positioned at (0, 0). Walk the
win.frameElement chain up to the top-level window and accumulate each
enclosing frame's viewport offset so the returned rect is in the
top-level web view's coordinate space.

testPasswordControllerSupportsIFrameMessaging is the only test in ios/
that calls TapWebElementWithIdInFrame
(selectorWithElementID:inFrameWithIndex:).

Verified locally with testPasswordControllerSupportsIFrameMessaging:
- iPad Pro 11-inch (M5) (iOS 27.0): 3/3
- iPad Pro 11-inch (M5) (iOS 26.5): 3/3
- iPhone 17 Pro Max (iOS 27.0): 3/3
- iPhone 17 Pro Max (iOS 26.5): 3/3

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

[Remoting] Re-enable InvalidClientConnects test on macOS

Re-enable ChromotingHostServicesServerTest.
InvalidClientConnects_BindingCallbackIsNotCalled on macOS.

When ChromotingHostServicesServerTest was enabled on macOS in
https://crrev.com/c/6449861,
InvalidClientConnects_BindingCallbackIsNotCalled was disabled because
the client process hung waiting for MOJO_HANDLE_SIGNAL_PEER_CLOSED on
the extracted message pipe. On macOS,
named_mojo_ipc_server::ConnectToServer() sends a Mach send right to the
server's bootstrap port and returns a receive-only
PlatformChannelEndpoint to the client. When the server's validator
rejects the client, NamedMojoMessagePipeServer drops the peer send right
without sending a Mojo invitation or ChannelMac handshake. Previously, a
receive-only ChannelMac only registered for peer loss
(MACH_NOTIFY_DEAD_NAME) after receiving the peer's send right in the
handshake, so dropping the send right before the handshake never
notified the client channel that the peer disconnected.

https://crrev.com/c/8574184 updated ChannelMac to request
MACH_NOTIFY_NO_SENDERS prior to receiving the handshake, allowing the
client's IncomingInvitation to detect peer loss when the server drops
the rejected endpoint and signal MOJO_HANDLE_SIGNAL_PEER_CLOSED on the
extracted message pipe.

Verified by running ChromotingHostServicesServerTest.
InvalidClientConnects_BindingCallbackIsNotCalled 50 times in
remoting_unittests.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

audio: Use real audio sources in UserMediaClientTest

UserMediaClientTest is a renderer-side integration test of the
mediastream pipeline, but UserMediaProcessorUnderTest::CreateAudioSource
previously bypassed UserMediaProcessor::CreateAudioSource() for
DEVICE_AUDIO_CAPTURE and returned a MockLocalMediaStreamAudioSource with
custom state and callback logic to simulate a processed source.

Stub the lower blink::Platform::NewAudioCapturerSource() boundary with a
no-op FakeAudioCapturerSource instead and delegate DEVICE_AUDIO_CAPTURE
to the real UserMediaProcessor::CreateAudioSource().

What this gives us:
1. Exercises the real production code paths in
   UserMediaProcessor::CreateAudioSource(),
   MediaStreamAudioProcessingLayout, ProcessedLocalAudioSource, and
   LocalMediaStreamAudioSource instead of testing custom mock logic that
   duplicated NeedWebrtcAudioProcessing() and property tracking.
2. Independent per-source state: Previously, all
   MockLocalMediaStreamAudioSource instances read from a single
   UserMediaProcessorUnderTest::last_audio_processing_properties_ field,
   so opening a second audio source overwrote the first source's
   properties. Real ProcessedLocalAudioSource instances own their own
   properties and AudioServiceAudioProcessorProxy.
3. Real ProcessedLocalAudioSource::From() type identity: Because
   MockLocalMediaStreamAudioSource could not inherit from final
   ProcessedLocalAudioSource, ProcessedLocalAudioSource::From() returned
   nullptr in UserMediaProcessor::SelectAudioDeviceSettings() and
   InitializeAudioSourceObject(), skipping those branches in tests.
4. Valid audio format on started sources: Base
   MediaStreamAudioSource::EnsureSourceIsStarted() never called
   SetFormat(), causing reused sources to appear uninitialized and
   overwrite their initial MediaStreamSource capabilities.
5. Removes ~150 lines of processed-source simulation and callback
   plumbing from MockLocalMediaStreamAudioSource,
   UserMediaProcessorUnderTest, and UserMediaClientUnderTest, leaving
   MockLocalMediaStreamAudioSource as a minimal stub for desktop/display
   audio capture only.

[Public Transit] Deprecate ChromeTabUtils#fullyLoadUrlInNewTab()

Mark fullyLoadUrlInNewTab() @Deprecated and point to the Station way:
openFakeLinkToWebPage() for a tab in the same model, or
Journeys.createRegularTabsWithWebPages() / createIncognitoTabsWithWebPages().

[sandbox] Allow arch_prctl(ARCH_GET_UNTAG_MASK) in x64 seccomp policy

The V8 sandbox tags upper address bits and relies on tagged pointers
faulting when dereferenced without first being untagged. Hardware
pointer untagging features on x64 (such as Intel LAM and AMD UAI) can
mask out these upper bits during address translation, which would break
this invariant.

Because hardware address untagging is not yet widely available across
all processors and OSes (including CQ/CI bots), we want to detect any
enablement of this feature at runtime as early as possible. To do so in
sandboxed processes, V8 queries the current untag mask via
arch_prctl(ARCH_GET_UNTAG_MASK, &untag_mask) during sandbox
initialization.

This CL allows ARCH_GET_UNTAG_MASK (0x4001) in the x86_64 baseline
seccomp-bpf policies (Linux/ChromeOS and Android) while keeping all
other arch_prctl operations (such as ARCH_ENABLE_TAGGED_ADDR) blocked.
This is similar to allowing read-only queries like
PR_GET_TAGGED_ADDR_CTRL and PR_PAC_GET_ENABLED_KEYS on arm64, and the
kernel implementation of ARCH_GET_UNTAG_MASK is a single read:

  case ARCH_GET_UNTAG_MASK:
    return put_user(task->mm->context.untag_mask,
                    (unsigned long __user *)arg2);

TAG=agy

Low-Coverage-Reason: COVERAGE_UNDERREPORTED CLANG_PROFILING_INSIDE_SANDBOX short-circuits SyscallSets::IsPrctl in baseline_policy.cc on coverage builds.
