Disallow duplicate DECLARE_USER_DATA in class hierarchies

Declaring DECLARE_USER_DATA on both a base interface and a derived
implementation class in the same inheritance hierarchy shadows
Base::kDataKey with Derived::kDataKey. This causes
UserDataFactoryWithOwner::CreateInstance<Derived>() to look up overrides
under Derived::kDataKey while tests register overrides under
Base::kDataKey via AddOverrideForTesting(), silently bypassing test
overrides or registering instances under two separate
UnownedUserDataHost keys.

Add a compile-time concept SingleUnownedUserDataInHierarchy<T> that
detects duplicate DECLARE_USER_DATA declarations in a hierarchy via an
ADL consteval friend function (CheckSingleUnownedUserDataInHierarchy)
that becomes ambiguous when declared in both a base and derived class.
Enforce this concept via static_assert in ScopedUnownedUserData<T> and
UserDataFactoryWithOwner's CreateInstance,
CreateInstanceWithFactoryMethod, and AddOverrideForTesting.

Remove duplicate DECLARE_USER_DATA / DEFINE_USER_DATA declarations
across all 5 violating hierarchies in //chrome/browser by promoting
shared methods onto the base interfaces and migrating callers to
Base::From():
- SkillsUiTabController (: SkillsUiTabControllerInterface)
- ActorUiTabController and ActorUiTabControllerAndroid (:
  ActorUiTabControllerInterface)
- ContextualTasksSidePanelCoordinator (: ContextualTasksPanelController)
- SidePanelCoordinator and SidePanelCoordinatorAndroid (:
  SidePanelUIBase : SidePanelUI), keeping
  SidePanelCoordinatorAndroid::From() backed by a static map
- TranslateBubbleController (: TranslateController)

[Indigo] Keep IndigoContextMenu enabled in legacy test fixtures

Now that the context menu feature is enabled by default, the controller
delegates omnibox cueing to Contextual Cueing V2 whenever Contextual
Cueing V2 is enabled. Consequently, the non-delegated legacy page action
path is only reached when Contextual Cueing V2 is disabled, in which
case proactive contextual cues are never permitted and eligible
navigations always show the suggestion chip rather than a proactive
anchored message.

This updates the legacy test fixtures to disable Contextual Cueing V2
instead of the context menu feature. Navigation helpers in legacy mode
now expect the suggestion chip on navigation and click it to open the
reactive anchored message. Tests that previously performed an extra
initial navigation solely to exhaust the proactive cue cooldown now
navigate once directly to the suggestion chip, and unit tests that
specifically exercised the now-unreachable legacy proactive anchored
message path are removed.

[Extensions] Allow runtime messaging from webview-accessible resources

When a Chrome App or extension navigates a <webview> guest to a
webview-accessible extension resource (chrome-extension://<id>/...), the
guest process is intentionally excluded from ProcessMap and classified
as an unprivileged extension context
(ContextType::kUnprivilegedExtension).
However, runtime messaging APIs (such as runtime.sendMessage and
runtime.connect) are exposed to unprivileged extension contexts.

Recent checks in IsValidMessagingSource() and IsValidSourceUrl() assumed
that any renderer process hosting an extension origin that is not in
ProcessMap must be a manifest-sandboxed extension frame, resulting in
false-positive renderer kills when a <webview> guest on an accessible
resource sent a runtime message.

Update checks in the messaging bindings to also allow non-sandboxed
<webview> guest processes owned by the extension when opening a channel
to an extension (while keeping tab and native messaging restricted to
privileged extension processes).

Reland "[fonts] Speed up FontFamilyCache::FillFontFamilyMap"

This is a reland of commit 73d8aaf2c72ff76ccc6b2830175cc0227395f76c

In the original CL and this reland, FontFamilyCache::FillFontFamilyMap
overwrites the output ScriptFontFamilyMap (*map = it->second) instead of
inserting non-empty entries into the map pre-populated by
WebPreferences() [1]. The original CL was reverted
(https://crrev.com/c/8594878) out of concern that overwriting *map would
discard pre-populated "Zyyy" (kCommonScript) defaults.

On closer inspection, in normal operation overwriting *map preserves
kCommonScript ("Zyyy") because:
- PrefsTabHelper::RegisterProfilePrefs registers non-empty localized
  defaults (IDS_*_FONT_FAMILY) [2] for all 7 "Zyyy" font preferences
  (kFontDefaults) [3].
- Its browser_script != pref_script check [4] never skips "Zyyy", since
  GetScriptOfBrowserLocale [5] never returns USCRIPT_COMMON.

However, an extension can set a "Zyyy" preference to "" via
chrome.fontSettings.setFont [6]. Before https://crrev.com/c/8463122,
FillFontFamilyMap ignored empty prefs [7], falling back to the hardcoded
font in WebPreferences() [1]; in https://crrev.com/c/8463122, it left
"Zyyy" unset in *map, leaving Blink's GenericFontFamilySettings without
a USCRIPT_COMMON fallback font on new WebViews (or retaining the old
"Zyyy" font on existing WebViews in ApplyFontsFromMap [8]).

Changes relative to the original CL (https://crrev.com/c/8463122):
1. Falls back to prefs_->GetDefaultPrefValue(pref_name) in
   FontFamilyCache::FetchFont when a "Zyyy" pref is empty, and CHECKs in
   FillFontFamilyMap that kCommonScript is populated. This is better
   than the pre-8463122 state: setting "" for "Zyyy" now uses the
   localized default from PrefService [2] (like clearFont) instead of
   the unlocalized font hardcoded in WebPreferences() [1].
2. Extends FontFamilyCacheTest to test setting/clearing cached prefs and
   verify that all 7 maps populate kCommonScript with the default pref
   value (even when set to ""), and adds
   PrefsTabHelperBrowserTest.FontFamilyPreferencesEndToEndRendering
   using DevTools CSS.getPlatformFontsForNode to verify that "Zyyy" and
   per-script ("Latn") font prefs take effect in Blink rendering.
3. Keeps blink::web_pref::ScriptFontFamilyMap as std::map (deferring the
   base::flat_map change to a separate CL).

[1] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/common/web_preferences/web_preferences.cc;l=24-42;drc=af3d5878bbb77212688848596b90b3d3e38a8cd5
[2] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:chrome/browser/ui/prefs/prefs_tab_helper.cc;l=427-465;drc=af3d5878bbb77212688848596b90b3d3e38a8cd5
[3] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:chrome/browser/ui/prefs/prefs_tab_helper.cc;l=147-154;drc=af3d5878bbb77212688848596b90b3d3e38a8cd5
[4] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:chrome/browser/ui/prefs/prefs_tab_helper.cc;l=451;drc=af3d5878bbb77212688848596b90b3d3e38a8cd5
[5] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:chrome/browser/ui/prefs/prefs_tab_helper.cc;l=252-281;drc=af3d5878bbb77212688848596b90b3d3e38a8cd5
[6] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:chrome/browser/extensions/api/font_settings/font_settings_api.cc;l=108-111;drc=af3d5878bbb77212688848596b90b3d3e38a8cd5
[7] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:chrome/browser/font_family_cache.cc;l=57-58;drc=29e5b5f877ed1ef4ad13032a23ff300c0f2b7322
[8] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/exported/web_view_impl.cc;l=336-346;drc=af3d5878bbb77212688848596b90b3d3e38a8cd5

Original change's description:
> [fonts] Speed up FontFamilyCache::FillFontFamilyMap
>
> See jank flame graph: go/flame-jank-fillfontfamilymap-20260925
>
> Previously, FontFamilyCache cached individual (map_name, script) ->
> std::u16string entries across a two-level std::unordered_map (1,064 [1]
> entries per profile, of which only 24 to 40 [2] have non-empty default
> values). Every call to WebContentsImpl::ComputeWebPreferences iterated
> over all 152 [3] scripts for each of the 7 [4] generic font families,
> performing 2,128 [5] hash lookups and rebuilding seven
> std::map<std::string, std::u16string> instances node-by-node.
>
> This CL optimizes font preference caching and copying:
> 1. Changes blink::web_pref::ScriptFontFamilyMap from std::map to
>    base::flat_map so copying each map requires a single contiguous
>    allocation rather than per-node tree allocations.
> 2. Caches the constructed ScriptFontFamilyMap (containing only non-empty
>    script entries) per font family in an
>    absl::flat_hash_map<std::string, ScriptFontFamilyMap>, making
>    warm-cache FillFontFamilyMap calls a single heterogeneous hash lookup
>    and flat_map copy.
> 3. Replaces base::StringPrintf in FontFamilyCache::FetchFont with a
>    stack-allocated buffer to avoid 1,064 heap allocations during cold
>    cache population.
>
> [1] 7 generic font families [4] * 152 scripts [3] = 1,064 font prefs.
> [2] kFontDefaults in chrome/browser/ui/prefs/prefs_tab_helper.cc
>     registers 24 (Linux), 26 (macOS), 30 (ChromeOS), or 40 (Windows)
>     non-empty default font prefs; RegisterFontFamilyPrefs registers the
>     remaining 1,024 to 1,040 prefs with an empty std::string().
> [3] ALL_FONT_SCRIPTS in chrome/common/pref_font_script_names-inl.h
>     expands to 152 ISO 15924 scripts
>     (prefs::kWebKitScriptsForFontFamilyMapsLength == 152).
> [4] ChromeContentBrowserClient::OverrideWebPreferences calls
>     FontFamilyCache::FillFontFamilyMap for 7 maps: standard, fixed,
>     serif, sans_serif, cursive, fantasy, and math.
> [5] FetchAndCacheFont performed 1 outer-map lookup + 1 inner-map lookup
>     per (map_name, script) pair: 2 * 1,064 = 2,128 lookups.
>

[a11y] Avoid unnecessary AddRef/Release during Windows atomic updates

https://crrev.com/c/8595191 added temporary `ComPtr` references in
`BrowserAccessibilityWin::UpdatePlatformAttributes()` and
`BrowserAccessibilityManagerWin::OnAtomicUpdateFinished()` to keep COM
nodes alive if an in-context WinEvent hook destroys a node while firing
events in `UpdateStep3FireEvents()`.

However, `UpdateStep1ComputeWinAttributes()` and
`UpdateStep2ComputeHypertext()` do not fire native events, and in
`UpdateStep3FireEvents()` most nodes updated during an atomic update do
not fire any WinEvents via `FireNativeEvent()`. In
`AXPlatformNodeWin::AddRef()` and `Release()`, every 1 -> 2 and 2 -> 1
reference count transition on a dormant node updates global dormant/live
node counts and invokes `OnReferenced()`/`OnDereferenced()`, which emit
instant trace events in the `"accessibility"` category. In addition,
`OnAtomicUpdateFinished()` allocated a `std::vector<ComPtr<...>>` for
all updated nodes. Acquiring and releasing two temporary `ComPtr`
references per updated node caused a 10-12% regression in
`OnAccessibilityEvents` on Windows.

To fix the regression while preserving lifetime safety:
- Move the temporary `ComPtr<BrowserAccessibilityComWin>` into
  `BrowserAccessibilityComWin::UpdateStep3FireEvents()` and acquire it
  lazily immediately before calling `FireNativeEvent()`.
- Check `if (IsDestroyed() || !update_state_)` after each
  `FireNativeEvent()` call and update `previous_scroll_x_`/
  `previous_scroll_y_` before `FireNativeEvent()` so re-entrant atomic
  updates that modify the firing node in place do not leave dangling
  references or clobber scroll state.
- Remove `com_objs_to_update` in
  `BrowserAccessibilityManagerWin::OnAtomicUpdateFinished()`. Instead,
  record `node_ids_to_update` during Step 1 and re-lookup each node via
  `GetFromID(id)` in Step 3 so sibling nodes destroyed by a synchronous
  WinEvent hook are safely skipped.
- Reset `update_state_ = nullptr` in
  `BrowserAccessibilityComWin::Destroy()` before calling
  `AXPlatformNodeWin::Destroy()`.

AX-Relnotes: n/a.

[iOS] Fix flakiness in GaiaAuthFetcherIOSNSURLSessionBridgeTest

This CL fixes flakiness in GaiaAuthFetcherIOSNSURLSessionBridgeTest and
re-enables FetchWithEmptyCookieStore, FetchWithCookieStore, and
FetchWithRedirect.

Previously, GaiaAuthFetcherIOSNSURLSessionBridgeTest::SetUp() created a
real NSURLSessionDataTask on [NSURLSession sharedSession] targeting
https://www.example.com and quit the RunLoop in FetchURL() from the
task's network completion handler. When [url_session_data_task_ resume]
was called by GaiaAuthFetcherIOSNSURLSessionBridge, it performed an
actual network request to https://www.example.com and waited for that
external request to complete or fail before returning from FetchURL().

Because -[NSHTTPCookieStorage storeCookies:forTask:] invokes internal
CFNetwork selectors on the task and OCMock cannot partially mock the
toll-free bridged __NSCFLocalDataTask class, this CL wraps the
unresumed NSURLSessionDataTask in FakeNSURLSessionDataTask, which
forwards internal selectors to the underlying task while intercepting
-resume (to quit the RunLoop immediately without starting a network
request) and -cancel.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

[perf] Disable system_health_smoke_test on 64-bit Android emulators

SystemHealthBenchmarkSmokeTest fails every time on
android-17-x64-fyi-rel and android-canary-x64-fyi-rel. Before starting
the browser, Telemetry flushes OS page caches with the
clear_system_cache helper. There is no clear_system_cache binary for
android_x86_64 in catapult's binary_dependencies.json, so every story
fails with NoPathFoundError.

Disable the smoke test on the android-sdk-gphone64-x86-64 typ tag until
clear_system_cache works on x64 emulators (tracked in b/578069352).
32-bit x86 emulators and arm devices are not affected.

b7b08909c5b8857222ad9884d9cfe5c75d0139a1 [ diff ] 
SVG text: clarify typographic character detection

Follow-up to crrev.com/c/8644950. The code says "typographic character"
but detects only the Grapheme_Extend subset of EGC continuations. Per
the SVG text layout algorithm, repositioning applies to typographic
characters, and the SVG spec cites "e.g. a ligature" as an example of
a typographic character spanning more than one character. Per CSS Text
3, the typographic character is based on the extended grapheme cluster
and tailored per typographic operation. The Grapheme_Extend check does
not detect ligatures or those tailorings. Call that out so the
terminology matches what the code actually tests and the implementation
gap (ligatures, non-combining-mark EGC continuations, tailorings) is
explicit.

[UI] Migrate components/omnibox to `ui::mojom::WindowOpenDisposition`

Spell the type as `ui::mojom::WindowOpenDisposition` instead of the
deprecated `WindowOpenDisposition` alias, and include
"ui/base/mojom/window_open_disposition.mojom.h" instead of
"ui/base/window_open_disposition.h".

Also migrate the few files outside components/omnibox that use the alias
but only got it through a components/omnibox header, so that they keep
compiling.

Initialize `TestOmniboxClient::last_log_disposition_` with a default
member initializer instead of in the constructor, as clang-tidy asks.

Headers that only use the type in declarations include the mojom
forward header instead of the full one.

No behavior change.

The rest of this CL was generated by running the following from
src/, then `git cl format`:

  migrate_window_open_disposition.py --migrate-type components/omnibox
  check_alias_includes.py --migrate

The scripts are attached to https://crbug.com/373551504.

OmniboxClient::OpenUrl() already had a default argument; this CL only
changes the spelling of its type, so skip google-default-arguments.

[rust] Use `chromium::import!` for `//components` Rust crates.

Before this CL, `//components/cbor/rust:cbor`,
`//components/web_package/rust:web_package_rust`, and
`//components/web_package/signed_web_bundles/rust` (target
`:signed_web_bundles_rust`) used an explicit `crate_name`.  This
bypasses the auto-generated, globally unique crate name.  For example,
`crate_name = "cbor"` collides with `third_party/cloud_authenticator`'s
`cbor` crate.

After this CL, these targets use the default crate name, and the Rust
code in `//components/cbor` and `//components/web_package` imports them
with `chromium::import!`.  This CL does not change behavior.
